classification.difficultyReason: Translate a three-sided fencing constraint into an area inequality, solve it and interpret the smallest feasible dimension.

content.prompt: A farmer needs to build a rectangular holding pen for some sheep. The side of a barn will be used for one side of the pen and there is $60\text{ m}$ of fencing available for the remaining three sides. Let $x$ be the length of each side perpendicular to the barn wall.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find an expression for the third side in terms of $x$ and draw a diagram showing all this information.

answer.worked:
Let the third side have length $L$ metres.
$$\begin{align*}2x+L&=60\\L&=60-2x\end{align*}$$
The barn wall forms the fourth side; fencing is needed on the two sides of length $x$ and the side of length $60-2x$.

spec.description: Rectangular pen with the barn wall along the upper side, two perpendicular fenced sides and the remaining fenced side labelled. Decorative brickwork omitted.
spec.mathematics: The three fenced sides total x+x+(60-2x)=60 metres.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The area $A$ of the pen must be at least $400\text{ m}^2$ so that the sheep are not overcrowded. What is the smallest value of $x$ for these requirements?

answer.short:
$10\text{ m}$.

The area requirement holds for $10\le x\le20$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}A&=x(60-2x)\\x(60-2x)&\ge400\\60x-2x^2&\ge400\\x^2-30x+200&\le0\\(x-10)(x-20)&\le0\end{align*}$$
The zeroes are $10$ and $20$. The graph of $y=(x-10)(x-20)$ is an upward-opening parabola, so it is on or below the $x$-axis between its zeroes. Hence $10\le x\le20$. These values also satisfy the physical restriction $0<x<30$.

The smallest value is therefore $x=10\text{ m}$. At this value, the third side is $40\text{ m}$ and the area is $400\text{ m}^2$.

spec.description: Authored solution sketch applying the source-taught graphical method; roots labelled 10 and 20.
